summary: Remote-controlled daemon exposes shell/PTY and RDP/VNC to hardcoded WebSocket gateway
details: @whalent/agent is a daemon that connects to a WebSocket gateway (default memory.whalent.com, overridable via --gateway/WHALENT_GATEWAY) and accepts remote commands from that gateway. The bundle embeds node-pty for interactive shell/PTY dispatch and proxies RDP (port 3389) and VNC (ports 5900/5901) via guacd, giving whoever controls the gateway shell execution and desktop control on the host running the daemon. The main entry dist/index.cjs (114 KB) and dist/core.cjs (13.6 MB) are shipped through javascript-obfuscator with string-array rotation, control-flow flattening, and hex-encoded identifiers (_0x…); the package's own devDependencies list javascript-obfuscator ^5.3.0. The obfuscation covers the code paths that receive and dispatch remote gateway messages, so the full set of remote-invocable operations cannot be enumerated from the shipped code without deobfuscation. Even framed as a first-party remote-management agent, running `whalent --token …` yields full-host remote control (shell + desktop) to the party operating the gateway.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
